surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Still no win for the Flyers
paras: Matvei Michkov struck first for the Flyers late in the first, but they didn’t score again. Anton Johansson, in his seventh NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Dylan Larkin, early in the second to tie it 1-1. Andrew Copp put the Red Wings ahead for good with less than five minutes left.

The Red Wings drove the play, outshooting the Flyers 26-18, and the scoreboard caught up. Daniil Tarasov needed only 17 saves for the Red Wings, and Joseph Woll kept the Flyers in it, stopping 24 of 26. The Wings moved to 2-3-2, still last in the Atlantic. The Flyers are still last in the Metropolitan. The Flyers are still looking for their first win of the season, now 0-6-3.

items.text: The Red Wings won for the first time in four games.
Andrew Copp scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 19 (19 games played since).
Both of the preview’s calls held.
